feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A contract is not defined by its physical form; it is a legal and semantic structure.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — Entirely human-constructed and institutional in origin.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not derived from biological processes.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not mechanically or electrically activated.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not a structural element in the physical sense.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — While it can be seen, its identity lies in abstraction and legal recognition.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — It may exist in physical or digital form, but is not medium-defined.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Has no autonomous function; its power derives from human recognition and enforcement.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Crafted to represent the mutual agreement of obligations, compensation, and authority.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Triggers legal and economic processes but does not produce them independently.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Encodes logic symbolically but does not process or compute.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Symbolically represents a change of state (employment) but does not perform it autonomously.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Signed and reviewed by people, but not an interactive system.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used in systems (e.g., HR), but not an embedded component.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Requires institutional and legal context.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Employment can exist without formal contracts (e.g., informal or at-will labor).
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Represents mutual agreement and formalized authority.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Serves as institutional proof of employment, status, and authorization.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Subject to legal frameworks and formatting conventions.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Structured in clauses: roles, salary, duration, termination, etc.
feedback.Normative: Included — Encodes expected behaviors and institutional commitments.
feedback.Meta: Included — Refers to systems of classification, performance, and identity.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Defined by time: start date, term, renewal, probation period.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Predominantly stored and executed in digital HR systems.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists only through shared institutional and legal meaning.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized by HR departments, labor law, and legal conventions.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Defines role and status within an organization.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Bound by employment law and compliance requirements.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Establishes pay, benefits, and economic dependency.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Central in debates over labor rights, flexibility, and gig work.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Signing marks initiation into a role; often ceremonially staged.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Key to justice in employment, equity, and access.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the employment contract as a symbolic, structured, and temporally defined social artifact. It operates as both a legal instrument and a communicative ritual, deeply embedded in economic systems and ethical discourse.
